title: High churn detected in specific industries
summary: Average churn rate: 23.5%. High-churn industries: healthcare (32.4%)
narrative: Our overall customer churn rate stands at 23.5%, but healthcare clients are churning at 32.4%—nearly 9 percentage points above average, representing a significant retention problem in this vertical. This elevated healthcare churn could indicate issues with product-market fit, implementation challenges, or unmet regulatory requirements specific to this industry. I recommend conducting exit interviews with recent healthcare churns and analyzing their usage patterns to identify whether we need specialized onboarding, compliance features, or dedicated healthcare customer success resources.

title: Revenue concentration risk
summary: Enterprise plan drives 78.2% of total MRR.
narrative: Our revenue is heavily concentrated, with the Enterprise plan generating 78.2% of total monthly recurring revenue, which creates significant risk if we lose even one or two large customers. This dependency means a single churn event could materially impact our financial performance and make growth targets harder to achieve. We should immediately prioritize diversifying our revenue base by accelerating customer acquisition in the mid-market segment and developing new product tiers that reduce reliance on Enterprise customers.

title: Product engagement gap across plans
summary: Engagement gap: enterprise customers average 43.1 events/user vs growth at 38.0 events/user.
narrative: Enterprise customers are engaging 13% more actively than Growth plan users, averaging 43.1 events per user compared to 38.0 events on Growth plans. This gap suggests either that enterprise features are driving more valuable interactions or that Growth users may be hitting limitations that prevent deeper engagement. Conduct user interviews with high-activity Growth customers to identify which enterprise features they need most, then consider selectively exposing 1-2 of these capabilities to boost Growth plan engagement and create a clearer upgrade path.

title: Revenue concentration risk
summary: Enterprise plan drives 78.2% of total MRR.
narrative: Our revenue is heavily concentrated, with the Enterprise plan generating 78.2% of monthly recurring revenue while other plan tiers contribute just 21.8% combined. This creates significant vulnerability if we lose even one or two major enterprise customers, or if market conditions force enterprise buyers to downgrade. We should immediately launch an initiative to diversify revenue by either introducing a compelling mid-tier plan or investing in sales resources to acquire 15-20 additional mid-market customers over the next two quarters.

title: Product engagement gap across plans
summary: Engagement gap: enterprise customers average 43.1 events/user vs growth at 38.0 events/user.
narrative: Our enterprise customers are 13% more engaged than growth plan users, averaging 43.1 events per user compared to 38.0 events for growth tier. This suggests either that enterprise features are driving meaningful adoption or that high-engagement users naturally graduate to enterprise plans. We should analyze which specific enterprise features correlate with this increased activity to determine whether we can surface similar functionality in growth plans to boost engagement and potentially accelerate upgrades.
